curatorNotes:
I checked every selected topic's prerequisites against the existing catalogue and the selection. Three chains are broken, and I fixed them with notes rather than swaps, because each fix would cost a stronger topic.
- ising-model lists partition-function (runner-up, L3), which is not selected.
- turing-patterns lists morphogen-gradients (runner-up, L3), which is not selected.
- shapes-that-tile lists angles-as-turns (pool, L0, scores 3/4), which is not selected.
In each case the page can teach the missing idea in a step of its own, so I recommend dropping that prerequisite from the entry. If you would rather keep the chains whole, the alternative is to swap luria-delbruck for morphogen-gradients and to bring in partition-function in place of a weaker physics or chemistry L3.

AI balance after the swaps: AI holds 17 topics (9 ladder rungs, plus mixture-of-experts, weight-quantization and adaptive-optimizers, 3 at level 0 and 2 at level 1). Together with the existing embeddings, transformers, language-models and gradient-descent pages, the ladder now runs tokenizer, embeddings, position, attention, residual block, optimizer, training, scaling, RLHF, reasoning, then serving (KV cache, speculative decoding, quantization) and MoE architecture. That leaves one AI slot under the cap of 18. monte-carlo-tree-search (5/5, the top runner-up, and the natural sequel to the selected game-tree-search) is the obvious use for it, but it is not an LLM stage, so I did not force it in.

Level counts are unchanged, because every swap keeps its level. Category totals change: space and energy each lose L3 picks to AI, and chemistry loses an L0 to earth. If chemistry should keep three L0 pages, use salt-and-ice from the wider pool instead of beach-waves.

I did not swap kalman-filter in networks, though it fits that category oddly, nor monty-hall at L0: both are famous and score well.

selected.title: Tokenization & byte-pair encoding
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: Building BPE merge by merge and running GPT-2's real merges explains why tokens fall where they do, which goes beyond language-models' display of a given split.

build 5: BPE training on a typed corpus is a small exact algorithm and GPT-2's byte-level tokenizer (regex pre-split plus about 50k merges, a few hundred KB, MIT/modified-MIT) runs instantly in the browser.

selected.title: Training a tiny language model
judgeNotes: fit-level 5: A cornerstone level-3 LLM page: real cross-entropy training measured against n-gram baselines, with overfitting visible. Nothing existing trains a language model, and several other candidates build on it.

build 4: A two-layer character transformer with tens of thousands of weights can train live in JS or WebGPU at a few steps per frame, with honest loss curves. The overfitting and data-size sweeps may need precomputed runs to stay interactive; this page is also the infrastructure several other candidates depend on.

selected.title: Position in a transformer: sinusoids & RoPE
judgeNotes: fit-level 5: A clean, visual mechanism (order-blind attention, then sinusoids and RoPE rotations) that the transformers page never covers; honest level 3 with the real math.
build 5: Pure math needing no data: permutation equivariance of attention, sinusoidal encodings and RoPE's relative-distance invariance are exact, small computations that render instantly.

selected.title: Inside a transformer block: the residual stream
judgeNotes: fit-level 5: It shows the whole transformer block, residual sum and MLP, with predictions read out at every depth, which the attention-only transformers page leaves out; it is core to understanding LLMs in detail.

build 4: Precomputed GPT-2 small activations for a fixed prompt set (modified MIT), with the 24 single-component ablations per prompt, are a modest dataset and give a real logit-lens grid. Free-text prompts would need ONNX GPT-2 in the browser (around 100+ MB), so precomputed is the practical route.

selected.title: Scaling laws
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: An empirical law, not a causal mechanism, but the Chinchilla compute-optimal split is a real model the graphic can solve; the live retraining is heavy and adds little.

build 4: The precomputed sweep of the project's own small models and the Chinchilla parametric law with published constants are honest and cheap to render; retraining one sweep point live must be a tiny model to stay interactive, and Epoch AI data should be dropped unless its licence is checked.

selected.title: RLHF: learning from human preferences
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: A well-designed level-3 page: a Bradley-Terry reward model plus an exact KL-tilted policy makes reward hacking visible, and it is clearly distinct from grid-world reinforcement learning.

build 4: The Bradley-Terry fit on precomputed embeddings and the exact KL-tilted policy over 64 precomputed GPT-2 continuations are small, honest computations, and reward hacking falls out of the real math; GPT-2 and MiniLM licences are open.

selected.title: Why thinking out loud helps a model
judgeNotes: fit-level 5: It shows on a checkable addition task why fixed compute per token makes written working help, a distinctive and timely mechanism that no page covers.

build 3: Training two tiny addition transformers offline is doable, but the outcome is an empirical result that has to be measured, not asserted. Tiny transformers often learn direct addition fine at trained lengths and fail length generalisation even with a scratchpad unless positions are handled carefully, so the claim about lengths beyond training is at risk.

selected.title: Serving a language model: the KV cache
judgeNotes: fit-level 5: It explains with a real roofline model why decoding is memory-bound and why batching makes serving cheap; this is distinct from the gpu page's parallel speed-up race and essential to how LLMs are run.

build 4: The cache-versus-recompute FLOP and byte counts and the roofline from published datasheet and model-card figures are exact arithmetic. Live wall-clock timing in the browser is noisy, though, so the takeaway should rest on the counted operations, not on measured times.

selected.title: Speculative decoding
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: The rejection-sampling rule and its histogram that matches the target exactly make an elegant, checkable mechanism, distinct from kv-cache-inference, which it builds on.

build 5: The accept/reject rule with residual resampling is an exact algorithm on two small own models (or even on toy distributions), and the 10,000-sample histogram matching the target is a clean, honest demonstration.

selected.title: Phase portraits & stability
judgeNotes: build 5: Eigenvalues of a 2×2 matrix, a trace–determinant chart, a streamline field and RK4 trajectories for the pendulum, predator–prey and van der Pol systems through a Hopf bifurcation all run live, with no data.

fit-level 4: Classifying flows by eigenvalues on the trace-determinant chart, with linearizations laid over real flows and a Hopf bifurcation, is the standard university model. It is distinct from chaos-fractals and ecosystems.

selected.title: The brachistochrone & calculus of variations
judgeNotes: build 5: The bead's descent time is a 1D quadrature along a spline, and gradient descent on a dozen control points converging to the analytic cycloid (plus the catenary) runs at interactive rates; this is the real functional being minimised.

fit-level 4: The brachistochrone race is a classic, visual, wanted subject, and relaxing a curve toward the cycloid shows the real functional being minimized. That is honest level-3 content and distinct from newtons-laws.

selected.title: Random graphs & the giant component
judgeNotes: build 5: Erdős–Rényi graphs on a few hundred nodes with union-find for the giant component, preferential attachment and grid bond percolation are cheap seeded simulations, and the threshold appears in the live plot.

fit-level 4: The giant component's sudden appearance at average degree 1 is a striking emergent mechanism, and preferential attachment adds real network science. No existing page covers network structure itself.

selected.title: Taylor series & where they stop working
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: Showing the radius of convergence set by a complex singularity is a real and surprising mechanism; plain Taylor polynomials would be level 2, but the complex-disk explanation makes level 3 honest, and it is distinct from calculus.
build 5: Partial sums, the disk of convergence reaching the singularities at ±i, and Chebyshev interpolation are exact cheap computations, and blow-up beyond |x| = 1 is visible at a glance.

selected.title: Hypothesis tests, the bootstrap & permutation
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: Permutation tests, the bootstrap and power are real university statistics with a mechanism the graphic shows directly (rebuilding the null distribution), and the page is clearly distinct from central-limit-theorem and learning-from-data.

build 5: Permutation tests, bootstrap and power curves are a few thousand cheap resamples of 344 rows, an honest algorithm at interactive rates; palmerpenguins is confirmed CC0 (the authors ask, as a courtesy and not a licence term, to be contacted before publication).

selected.title: Lasers
judgeNotes: fit-level 5: High visitor demand and a real rate-equation model (threshold, clamping, two-level saturation, Q-switching) that no existing page covers.
build 5: Four-level rate equations with a photon number are a small, stiff-but-easy ODE that shows threshold, clamping, relaxation oscillations and Q-switching honestly.

selected.title: Dislocations: why metals bend and alloys resist
judgeNotes: fit-level 5: Why metals yield far below bond strength is a striking, showable mechanism at the heart of materials science, and no existing page covers it.

build 4: 2D Lennard-Jones molecular dynamics of a few thousand atoms with an edge dislocation glides under shear at interactive rates and shows solute pinning, but convincing work-hardening pile-ups need more atoms than a browser box holds, so that last step should stay modest.

selected.title: Catalysis on a surface
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: The Ziff-Gulari-Barshad lattice model shows site coverage and CO poisoning, a mechanism the existing page's barrier-lowering catalyst never models.

build 5: The Ziff-Gulari-Barshad lattice model is a classic, cheap cellular simulation whose CO-poisoning transition emerges on its own, and adding desorption with temperature is a one-line extension. It needs no data.

selected.title: Molecular orbitals & conjugation
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: Diagonalizing Hückel matrices to explain dye colour and aromaticity is a real model with a visual payoff, and chemical-bonds' VSEPR picture does not cover it.

build 5: Diagonalizing a small Hückel adjacency matrix is exact and instant, the ring and chain level patterns and aromaticity show directly, and the cyanine absorption maxima are published facts; simple Hückel gets only the trend of the gap, not absolute colours, and the page should say so.

selected.title: Reaction trajectories & the transition state
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: Classical trajectories on a LEPS surface with Polanyi's early/late barrier rules and the kinetic isotope effect are the real university model behind the 1D profile on reaction-rates-equilibrium.

build 5: Classical trajectories on a LEPS surface for H+H2 and F+H2 are a textbook small ODE with published Sato parameters (facts). Polanyi's early/late barrier rules and Eyring rates follow directly. The zero-point-energy isotope effect must be added as a stated harmonic correction.

selected.title: X-ray diffraction: reading a crystal
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: Structure factors, Bragg peaks and systematic absences make a real, interactive Fourier-transform-of-a-crystal page not covered anywhere; the semiconductors prerequisite is weak and could be dropped.

build 5: Structure factors from Cromer-Mann coefficients, Bragg angles for a powder pattern and an Ewald-sphere construction are a small, honest computation, and editing the cell changes the intensities directly. COD entries are public domain/CC0, and the scattering coefficients are published facts (also in BSD xraylib).

selected.title: Turing patterns
judgeNotes: fit-level 5: Reaction-diffusion spots and stripes are a beautiful, widely sought mechanism driven by a real PDE, and they are distinct from chaos-fractals.

build 5: A Gierer-Meinhardt or Gray-Scott grid PDE runs at interactive rates in JS (or WebGL) and shows the diffusion-ratio threshold honestly; growing and tapered domains are a mask on the same grid.

selected.title: Population genetics: drift & selection
judgeNotes: fit-level 5: Wright-Fisher drift versus selection, with Kimura's fixation probability, is the core university model the evolution page lacks, and it is ideal for many live traces.
build 5: A hundred Wright-Fisher binomial traces per generation are cheap, and fixation near 2s and the Hardy-Weinberg ratios are exact checks; no data needed.

selected.title: Bacterial chemotaxis
judgeNotes: fit-level 5: A textbook university systems-biology model (run-and-tumble, Barkai-Leibler perfect adaptation) whose emergent drift up the gradient is exactly what an animated simulation shows best, and no page is like it.

build 5: A few hundred run-and-tumble agents, each running a small ODE for receptor methylation with exact adaptation, run comfortably in real time, and the drift up the gradient and the dip-and-recover under a uniform dose come out of the model itself.

selected.title: Gene regulation & the lac operon
judgeNotes: fit-level 5: The canonical model of gene regulation (Ozbudak et al.), with hysteresis and diauxie the toy shows, and it is the prerequisite other candidates rely on; it is distinct from dna-to-protein, and its prerequisite reaction-rates-equilibrium is at level 2, which suits level 3.

build 4: The Ozbudak-style bistable ODE gives the hysteresis loop honestly; showing the diauxic pause needs a separate growth-and-substrate model (Monod with catabolite repression) coupled to it, which is small but should be stated.

selected.title: Morphogen gradients & positional information
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: Covers the reserve item on pattern formation with a real diffusion-decay model and the French flag; it is distinct, but it should be planned together with turing-patterns and segmentation-clock so the three do not blur.
build 5: A 1D diffusion-decay PDE with thresholds is a small honest model with an analytic steady state to check against; the scaling mechanism needs one stated extra term.

selected.title: MRI: an image from spinning protons
judgeNotes: fit-level 5: medical-imaging only sketches MRI; the Bloch equations, the gradients and filling k-space make a distinct, visually striking level-3 page built on fourier-transform.

build 5: Bloch precession for the signal and a 2D FFT of an analytic Shepp–Logan phantom (line-by-line k-space filling and masking) are small, exact and fast; OpenNeuro data are CC0 if a real slice is wanted.

selected.title: The cerebellum & motor learning
judgeNotes: fit-level 5: Visuomotor rotation, with the reader's own hand fitted by the two-rate error-driven model and showing aftereffects and savings, is a real research model and an unforgettable interactive with no overlap.

build 5: Visuomotor rotation measured from the reader's own pointer, with the Smith-Shadmehr two-rate model fitted beside it, is a real experiment plus a tiny published model; aftereffect and savings emerge, and the VOR extension is optional.

selected.title: Hearing & the cochlea
judgeNotes: fit-level 5: The site has no hearing page; the place code (a travelling wave on a graded membrane) and the cochlear-implant finale make a strong, visual, distinct level-3 mechanism.

build 4: A frequency-domain 1D transmission-line cochlea and a band vocoder (Web Audio) for the implant are both cheap. The outer-hair-cell gain is a phenomenological negative damping and should be stated as one. A CC0 speech clip is easy to find.

selected.title: The ECG & arrhythmias
judgeNotes: fit-level 5: Computing the ECG from an excitable-medium model and breaking it into a spiral wave goes far past heart-circulation's synced trace, and it is a showcase mechanism at an honest level 3.

build 4: Aliev–Panfilov on a grid of about 150 by 150 runs spiral waves at interactive rates, a dipole projection gives an honest ECG, and MIT-BIH is ODC-By (verified on PhysioNet). Putting a conduction system and AV node on a 2D sheet is a hand-built approximation and should be presented as one.

selected.title: Weather forecasts: why they come as odds
judgeNotes: fit-level 5: A real mechanism (Lorenz-96 ensembles, spread against error, and the assimilation cycle) that people meet every day in forecasts; it starts where chaos-fractals stops and is honestly university atmospheric science.

build 5: Lorenz-96 with 40 variables is cheap enough that fifty RK4 members plus a small ensemble Kalman filter run easily in the browser; the model is the standard testbed forecasters use and needs no data.

selected.title: Radiative transfer & the climate column
judgeNotes: fit-level 5: The emission-height and lapse-rate column is the textbook university step beyond greenhouse-effect's zero-dimensional balance, and it explains stratospheric cooling with the real two-stream model.
build 5: A grey two-stream column with a window band and convective adjustment (Manabe-Wetherald style) is a classic tiny model that relaxes in milliseconds and needs no data.

selected.title: The carbonate-silicate thermostat
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: A genuine level-3 Walker-Hays-Kasting box model coupled to energy balance, with faint-Sun and snowball experiments; distinct from the fast carbon cycle over decades.
build 5: The Walker-Hays-Kasting weathering feedback with a one-layer energy balance is a two-variable ODE box model that integrates over millions of years in milliseconds and needs no data.

selected.title: Ocean acidification & carbonate chemistry
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: Seawater carbonate equilibria with saturation state and the Revelle factor are a real coupled model that acids-bases never reaches; the subject is in high demand and the level is honest.

build 5: Solving the seawater carbonate system with fixed alkalinity is a one-variable root find using published empirical constants (Lueker/Millero/Mucci fits, facts from the literature), which is the honest CO2SYS model and runs instantly.

selected.title: The three-body problem & Lagrange points
judgeNotes: fit-level 5: The rotating-frame CR3BP with Jacobi zero-velocity curves, tadpole orbits and chaotic divergence is a superb level-3 manipulate page that orbits-kepler does not reach.
build 5: The circular restricted three-body problem in the rotating frame, with Jacobi zero-velocity curves and RK integration of probes, is exact, small and fast.

selected.title: Interferometry & aperture synthesis
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: A genuine level-3 mechanism (uv coverage, dirty beam, CLEAN) built on fourier-transform, and distinct from the single-dish telescopes candidate.
build 5: Baselines tracing uv arcs, a gridded 2D FFT for the dirty beam and image, and Högbom CLEAN on a 128-256 pixel grid are small, exact and fast in the browser, with no data needed.

selected.title: Caches & the memory hierarchy
judgeNotes: fit-level 5: A cache simulator with real parameters, where row against column order changes the miss rate, is a core systems mechanism at the right level, with a strong visual and no overlap with cpu's flat memory.

judgeNotes: fit-level 4: It shows concretely, with chat templates, answer-only loss and side-by-side distributions, how a base model becomes an assistant, which is a key gap in the LLM story; showing behaviour needs two small open models in the browser.

judgeNotes: fit-level 4: Causal tracing is a real intervention with a clear heatmap and asks a different question from the logit lens (what causes recall, not what is readable). It is more specialised, but valuable for a detailed LLM series.

judgeNotes: fit-level 4: Matching ridge endings and forks against an 'enough' line is a clean level-0 mechanism on a familiar object, and nothing existing shows a biometric match; it is the stronger of the two biometric candidates.

judgeNotes: fit-level 4: It applies policy-gradient RL with group-relative advantages to a language model and shows pass@1 rising against pass@k, which is distinct from the grid-world RL page and central to modern reasoning models, though live GRPO in the browser is ambitious.

runnersUp.title: Bread and yeast

runnersUp.title: Why a cut apple goes brown
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: A familiar object with one-control experiments (acid, air, cold, heat) showing an enzyme at work is a good level-0 toy, though its 'heat destroys the enzyme' beat overlaps jelly-and-pineapple.

runnersUp.title: Zoom by tens

runnersUp.title: Auroras: the Sun's wind on Earth's magnet
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: Charged specks sliding along field lines into polar rings works without formulas and has one control and a well-known sky phenomenon; leadsTo should point to something nearer than atoms-periodic-table (for example sun-earth-moon), since electromagnetism is level 2.

runnersUp.title: Soap: surfactants & micelles

runnersUp.title: Tidal locking & orbital resonance
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: The secular tidal evolution into tidal locking and the Laplace resonance is a real long-timescale mechanism that sun-earth-moon's present-day tides do not show.

build 3: The secular tidal equations for spin and orbit are easy, but capturing the 2:1 chain and the Laplace resonance needs an orbit-resolving N-body run with a parametrised migration force and compressed timescales, which is buildable but harder to keep honest.

runnersUp.title: Water drops & surface tension
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: Beading, the coin bulge, the floating paperclip and soap are classic, hands-on surface-tension mechanics absent from states-of-matter; it is distinct from the sponge candidate if that one sticks to adhesion and capillarity.

build 3: A 2D molecular box with a free surface and a tunable wall attraction honestly shows beading and wetting, but the coin bulge, floating paperclip, pond skater and pepper are macroscopic effects that the particle box cannot reach at its scale, so those scenes need a separate Young-Laplace model or should be cut.

runnersUp.title: Zipper
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: Interlocking teeth and the slider's wedge are a visual, little-known mechanism a child handles daily; there is nothing like it on the site.

runnersUp.title: How plants drink

runnersUp.title: TLS: how a connection becomes private

judgeNotes: build 3: Tracking the roots numerically while the coefficients move and recording the permutation is buildable and honest, but Arnold's nested-commutator argument for degree 5 needs carefully precomputed loops, and the commutator depth is an argument the page shows rather than a model it computes, so this is a hard page to make legible.

runnersUp.title: Heat transfer: conduction, convection & radiation

Narrow it to the wall/insulation model with a U-value meter.

runnersUp.title: How a broken bone mends
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: A clear staged mechanism (haematoma, soft callus, hard callus, remodelling) with one honest control (cast vs movement) that a 10-year-old who has seen a cast will follow; distinct from bridges-structures and from the level-3 bone-remodelling candidate.

runnersUp.title: Mantle convection

runnersUp.title: Tap to pay

runnersUp.title: Cooking an egg

runnersUp.title: Why onions make you cry

judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Finding primes by trying rectangles is a nice level-0 way in, but its takeaway (which counts are prime and where they fall) largely repeats what primes-modular-arithmetic's sieve already shows.
build 4: Enumerating factor pairs to lay out chairs and lighting single-line counts on a hundred-square is a small exact algorithm that draws directly.

runnersUp.title: The segmentation clock
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The clock-and-wavefront model is a distinct, elegant mechanism, but it is a third pattern-formation page beside morphogen-gradients and turing-patterns and leans on a level-3 prerequisite.
build 4: A strip of Lewis delay-differential oscillators with Notch coupling and a moving wavefront is a small DDE system that runs interactively with a history buffer; no data needed.

runnersUp.title: Helicopters: a spinning wing
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The rotating wing, disc tilt and tail-rotor torque reaction are a genuine level-0 mechanism, but this is one of four wing-family candidates in the batch (with kite, paper plane and sailing), so it competes with them for a place.

build 4: Momentum-theory thrust from spin and collective, a tilted thrust vector and a yaw ODE for torque reaction make a small rigid-body sim that is honest at level 0, though blade-element detail must stay out.

runnersUp.title: Version control & Merkle trees
judgeNotes: build 4: Content hashing (SHA-1 or SHA-256 via SubtleCrypto), an object DAG, a Myers diff with three-way merge and Merkle proofs are all real and small, though the scope is broad.

fit-level 3: Content addressing, three-way merge and Merkle proofs are a real mechanism, but the hash-chain tamper demo partly repeats consensus-blockchains, and the page mixes two subjects (git and Merkle proofs).

runnersUp.title: Nuclear reaction networks in stars
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: A stiff reaction network with the temperature switch from pp to CNO is real level-3 content, but it partly overlaps stars (which fuses what) and nuclear-fusion, and it is heavy to build.
build 4: A roughly 15-species stiff network with Caughlan-Fowler analytic rates (published formulas) integrates quickly with an implicit solver; REACLIB has no confirmed licence, so use CF88.

runnersUp.title: Why a shot protects you
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: A head-start race of counts is an honest level-0 framing, but its takeaway (memory is already in place) is the same as mrna-vaccines and immune-system's second response, so it is a simpler retelling rather than a new mechanism.

build 4: Exponential pathogen growth racing a clonal expansion that starts from a handful versus thousands of memory cells is a tiny ODE with textbook timescales, and the head start is visible in the curves; honest at level 0.

runnersUp.title: Dams and water wheels: the push is in the height
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Height times flow as a comparison works at level 0 and is distinct from power-grid, but the mechanism is thin (one product of two quantities) and the waterfall and reservoir parts dilute it.

build 4: Torricelli outflow, power proportional to flow times head and a draining reservoir are a small honest model, and the equal-power comparison of high head against high flow comes straight out of it.

runnersUp.title: Car brakes
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Familiar and mechanistic, but it packs three ideas (lever, hydraulic multiplication, speed-squared stopping distance) into one level-0 page with one control at a time; it should be trimmed to the hydraulic chain or to stopping distance.

build 4: A lever, Pascal's-law hydraulic ratio, pad friction and v-squared stopping distance with a friction limit for skidding make a small honest chain of models, though it is two pages' worth of content and should be kept tight.

runnersUp.title: Colloids: why particles stay apart, and when they stick
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: DLVO stability and salt-induced flocculation are a genuine level-3 model with a nice real-world hook (river deltas), but niche, and it depends on the proposed dispersion-forces page.

build 4: Brownian dynamics of a few hundred particles under the DLVO pair potential (van der Waals plus screened double-layer repulsion with a Debye length set by salt and valence) runs easily in the browser, and flocculation and the strong valence dependence emerge from it; no data is needed.

runnersUp.title: Escalator
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: A neat geometric mechanism (rigid steps kept level by two offset tracks), but it is narrow, and leadsTo unit-circle is a stretch.

build 4: A real geometric construction (a rigid step on two wheel pairs riding two offset tracks) stays level, or tilts when the reader moves the tracks; the comb-and-groove zoom is the only part that is just a picture.

runnersUp.title: Metal detectors
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Eddy-current echoes are a real mechanism and an appealing device, but induction stretches what a 10-year-old can grasp without field ideas, and it should lead to electromagnetism more than to electric-circuits.

build 4: A search coil coupled to a target as a small RL loop, with mutual inductance falling off steeply with depth, is a small honest model that distinguishes conductors from a stone and shows the depth-versus-coil-size trade-off.

runnersUp.title: Feynman diagrams
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: High demand, and turning diagrams into a tree-level calculator checked against LEP data is a real mechanism well beyond standard-model's beta-decay step-through; it does lean on perturbation-theory, which is also in the pool.

build 2: No browser can evaluate amplitudes from an arbitrary drawn diagram, so the 'calculator' would be a lookup of a few closed-form cross sections; also, at 192-208 GeV LEP data are dominated by Z exchange, so pure QED would not match. HEPData is CC0, but record 48691 is the muon A_FB table, so the cross-section companion tables are also needed. Keep only if narrowed to a fixed set of processes with γ+Z formulas.

runnersUp.title: Smell and taste
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: The combinatorial receptor-pattern code and the pinched-nose test show a real mechanism a child can play with, a good level-0 sibling to vision-color without repeating it.

build 2: The receptor 'locks' are an invented toy matrix unless an open odorant-receptor response dataset (for example Pyrfume-hosted data, licence to be checked per set) fills it, and the pinched-nose strawberry is a picture to tap; the combinatorial-code idea survives only if the matrix comes from real data.

runnersUp.title: Why a photo cannot unlock your phone
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Structured-light depth sensing is a real mechanism a child can follow (photo fails, twin passes), but it is more optics than AI and overlaps fingerprint-match's 'enough points agree' takeaway in this batch, so the project should probably keep only one of the two biometric pages.

build 3: Ray-casting a dot pattern onto a parametric head and comparing depth maps is a real triangulation model and works without data. The match score and the twin case are toy stand-ins for a real face-ID network, though, so the page has to say the matcher is simplified.

runnersUp.title: Contrastive & self-supervised learning
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: A genuine level-3 mechanism distinct from embeddings, but training an image encoder live in the browser is heavy, and the CLIP add-on makes it two pages in one.

build 3: An InfoNCE encoder on a Fashion-MNIST subset (MIT) is feasible as precomputed checkpoints, but live training with augmentations is slow in the browser. The CLIP variant has no real text data behind it, so it would be a toy, and it should be cut or narrowed to label-name text.

runnersUp.title: Rust
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Water plus air plus salt is a familiar KS3 experiment, but the model is an empirical rate grid with no visible mechanism of why iron and oxygen combine, so the toy explains less than it shows.

build 3: A grid automaton with wetness- and salt-dependent rates is buildable, but the relative rates are loosely sourced and the electrochemical mechanism is hidden. Anchor the rates to published corrosivity categories (ISO 9223) rather than invented numbers.

runnersUp.title: Water pressure & hydraulics
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Pressure growing with depth and hydraulic force multiplication are honest level-0 ideas, but the page bundles two mechanisms and its hydraulic lift repeats the same step in fluid-pressure-buoyancy in this file.

build 3: Hydrostatics, Torricelli and Pascal are trivially buildable. However, the honest Torricelli model contradicts the interaction: jets landing at the bottle's base level reach furthest from the middle hole (range 2*sqrt(h(H-h))), not the lowest, so the bottle must stand on a raised support or the claim must change.

runnersUp.title: Friction, bearings & lubrication
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The page solves the Reynolds-equation pressure wedge and sweeps the Stribeck curve, a genuine mechanism that replaces newtons-laws' friction coefficient and fits an engineering level 3, but its everyday hook (oil) is undersold and its appeal is moderate.

build 3: The 1D Reynolds equation, or the Sommerfeld solution, gives an honest film pressure and hydrodynamic friction, but the boundary and mixed parts of the Stribeck curve are not in that model and would need an empirical asperity-contact blend (e.g. Greenwood-Williamson), and ISO 3448 itself is a paywalled standard, though grade viscosities and the Walther fit are widely published.

runnersUp.title: Allergy, IgE & anaphylaxis
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The bell-shaped crosslinking curve is a real but narrow mechanism; it shares its circulation-collapse ending with sepsis-inflammation, so one of the two is enough.

build 3: The bivalent-crosslinking equilibrium (Dembo–Goldstein) is honest and gives the bell curve. The histamine-to-blood-pressure circulation and desensitization are glued-on toy compartments with no sourced parameters, so half the page would be a dressed-up picture.

runnersUp.title: How a cut heals
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Platelet plug and scab under new skin is a real mechanism from an everyday experience and works at level 0, though the cut-depth and scab-picking controls make a thinner toy than its sibling healing candidates.

build 3: Platelet particles sticking at a leak until the flow stops is an honest, cheap simulation; the scab and the creeping skin cells are a second, mostly scripted grid, and 'pick the scab and it reopens' is a rule rather than a model, so the page is half model and half animation.

runnersUp.title: Where the work goes: exergy
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Its takeaway (the boiler, not the condenser, destroys most work potential) is a real level-3 insight, but a Grassmann diagram is accounting more than mechanism, and it depends on steam-power-cycles, a page that does not exist yet.

build 3: A steady-state Rankine/Brayton exergy balance with IAPWS-IF97 and NASA polynomials is computable live, and the sliders do recompute the Grassmann diagram. But the 'hover each component' framing leans towards browse-a-diagram, and the page shares its whole property engine with the steam and gas-turbine candidates.

runnersUp.title: What a remote control says
judgeNotes: build 3: An NEC protocol encoder and timing display plus a line-of-sight and reflection ray model is real but thin, and it risks becoming a stepped picture of a pulse train unless the reflection and blocking geometry carries the page.
fit-level 3: A charming level-0 object with a real protocol (NEC-style pulse gaps) and a phone-camera hook, but the mechanism is thin and overlaps the barcode and binary ideas.

runnersUp.title: Inside an egg
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The breathing shell and growing air pocket give it a real mechanism, but much of the page is a developmental timeline of facts and the humidity control is a modest toy.

build 3: Water loss through the shell can be modelled honestly with Fick diffusion against humidity (Ar and Rahn shell conductance, published facts). Embryo mass by day is available in an open-access table (PLOS ONE, PMC4821564, CC BY, E8-E20), so the data is not as weak as the entry says. Candling views and hatching remain largely drawn.

runnersUp.title: Hydroelectric turbines
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Euler's turbine equation with velocity triangles and the morph across specific speed is real turbomachinery the graphic can show, distinct from power-grid, though demand is moderate and the pumped-storage add-on widens it.

build 3: The Euler-equation velocity triangles and the Pelton half-jet-speed optimum are honest and computable. But the specific-speed morph from Pelton to Francis to Kaplan, and their efficiency-versus-load curves, would be drawn shapes and representative curves rather than a model, so that part is a picture.

runnersUp.title: Who eats whom
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The ten-fold pyramid of counts is a fair level-0 door, but ecosystems (level 1, no prerequisites) already builds food webs and removes species, so the distinct part is only the energy-loss pyramid.

build 3: The model is the 10% transfer arithmetic over a user-built graph: honest and buildable, but thin, verging on a drag-and-drop diagram with a calculator. Energy splitting across a web needs a stated rule to be more than counts.

runnersUp.title: Substitution mechanisms: SN1 and SN2
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: A core university organic mechanism with a real rate-law and stereochemistry payoff, but narrower appeal and an ambitious EVB surface, and it leans on the separately proposed transition-state-theory page.

build 3: An EVB surface with a solvent-stabilised ionic state is a legitimate toy, but because its parameters are tuned to textbook relative rates, it risks being a picture dressed as a model. Stereochemistry and the rate law would be largely scripted on top. A simpler two-path competition with calibrated barriers may be more honest, and the page should state the fit.

runnersUp.title: Sailing against the wind
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Sail-and-keel tacking upwind is a surprising and real mechanism, but it is hard to make honest without force vectors at level 0, and it is another wing-family candidate in this batch.

build 3: Sail and keel as two lift-drag foils with a boat ODE in heading and leeway is buildable, but getting realistic upwind behaviour and leeway without a keel needs tuned polars; it is honest if the polars are simplified and say so.

runnersUp.title: Scaling a recipe
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The squash-colour test of a ratio, with the add-one-of-each error shown, is a good level-0 toy, but it overlaps percent-off and fractions-fair-shares and is closer to classroom arithmetic than to how something works.

build 3: Proportional scaling and a colour computed from the concentrate fraction (a simple mixing or Beer-Lambert-style shade) are honest and small, though the recipe half is close to a bar chart of a multiplication.

runnersUp.title: Fractions: fair shares
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Honest level 0 and well aimed at a known misconception, but it is closer to teaching a definition than showing how something works, and it overlaps scaling-a-recipe and percent-off in this batch.

build 3: Buildable as equal-partition geometry with overlay comparison and a sharing division, but the model is thin and risks being a picture to tap unless the sharing step actually computes cuts and redistribution.

runnersUp.title: Knot theory
judgeNotes: build 3: The Kauffman bracket (2^n states) and tricolorability are cheap for diagrams of up to about 12 crossings, and diagrams can be hand-entered because KnotInfo has no explicit data licence; extracting a PD code from a freehand curve and doing Reidemeister moves by dragging are hard to build, so a picker plus scripted moves is the realistic version.

fit-level 3: Reidemeister moves leaving invariants unchanged is a genuine mechanism, and no page covers knots. The Jones polynomial is heavy for the graphic, and the topic is less of a how-it-works subject than most.

runnersUp.title: The solar system to scale
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Popular and well suited to level 0, but it shows scale and light-travel time rather than a mechanism, so it sits nearer a survey of facts than a 'how it works' page.

build 3: Buildable from the public-domain NSSDC fact sheet, with the light front as a pure function of time, but the model is just scaling and distance over c, so it leans toward a zoomable diagram; it is acceptable at level 0 only if the scale and light-time interaction carry it.

runnersUp.title: Hydraulic machines
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The orifice law, throttling heat and the hydraulic natural frequency form an honest level-3 model of a familiar machine (the excavator), but the build-a-circuit format and the controller tuning make it sprawling and partly repeat feedback-control.

build 3: An orifice-law plus oil-compressibility ODE for a valve-cylinder-load is a small, real model with the ringing visible. But a free-form circuit builder with an excavator arm is a large UI scope, so a fixed circuit with a few components would keep it honest and buildable.

runnersUp.title: Per cent: out of a hundred
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The shifting base and a cut followed by a matching rise that does not cancel are useful and honest at level 0, but it is a modest arithmetic idea that overlaps fractions-fair-shares and scaling-a-recipe.
build 3: Honest but nearly calculator-thin: a hundred-square and bars driven by price times rate; the cut-then-rise asymmetry gives it one real observable, so it is buildable if kept tight.

runnersUp.title: Carbon capture
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The minimum work of separation against dilution is a real thermodynamic model and a timely subject, but the absorber-stripper process plus the power-plant coupling risk turning the page into a process survey rather than one graphic.

build 3: The minimum-work-of-separation curve against concentration is a clean, honest formula. But the absorber/stripper 'step' is mostly a flowsheet whose numbers come from Kent-Eisenberg plus a lumped heat balance, so it is at risk of being a diagram with numbers unless the loading cycle is drawn as a computed equilibrium plot.

runnersUp.title: The first breath
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The pressure reversal at the first breath is a neat mechanism and distinct, but the subject is niche and it depends on haemoglobin-oxygen and partly reuses lung-gas-exchange from this batch.

build 3: Buildable as a small lumped resistance and compliance network, but the resistances need a published fetal lumped model (e.g. Pennati et al.) cited rather than invented; otherwise the page slides toward a stepped diagram with colours.

runnersUp.title: Build a joint
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: A build toy where joint shape limits reach is honest at level 0 and distinct from bridges-structures, but it leans towards a classification of joint types more than a single causal mechanism.

build 3: Forward kinematics with per-joint degrees of freedom and textbook ranges is honest and cheap, but reaching the nose, scratching the back and turning a key are 3D tasks that are awkward in 2D SVG, and 'a ball at the knee buckles' needs forces the stated model does not have.

runnersUp.title: The cosmic distance ladder
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The error propagation up the rungs is a good mechanism, but parallax, Cepheid calibration and the Hubble law are first-year material rather than level 3, and the page partly overlaps dark-energy-supernovae.

build 3: Propagating errors up the ladder is a simple, honest computation, but every rung's data has an unconfirmed licence (Gaia is free with credit, OGLE and SH0ES are unclear), so the dataset must be checked or cut to small retyped tables with citations before building.

runnersUp.title: What a smoke alarm senses
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Both sensing mechanisms are real and showable, but ionisation-chamber current capture is a stretch for a 10-year-old, and the page reads more like a device tour than one takeaway toy.

build 3: Ion drift and capture by smoke particles and light scattering onto a sensor can be an agent sim, but the flaming-versus-smouldering response difference depends on particle size distributions that a level-0 toy model would have to assume, so there is a risk of a picture with dots unless the size dependence of capture and scattering is actually modelled.

runnersUp.title: Treasure maps: coordinates & scale
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Honest level 0 and distinct from graph-search, but naming a spot with two numbers and reading a scale bar is mostly a definition, with little mechanism for the graphic to show.
build 3: Ordered-pair placement and polyline length times a scale factor are honest but thin computations; buildable, with the scale-invariance step the only real model behaviour.

runnersUp.title: Why you feel full
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Stomach stretch and gastric emptying rates give a genuine, formula-free mechanism with a nice same-energy comparison, distinct from homeostasis's blood-sugar loop, though the satiety story is simplified (hormones are left out) and the page must not overclaim.

build 3: Gastric emptying by food type is a small compartment model with published half-times, but the fullness gauge is an invented function of volume plus a gut signal, and the soup-versus-snack takeaway rests entirely on that invented weighting; it needs a cited satiety relation to count as a model.

runnersUp.title: Sea-level fingerprints
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The sea-level equation's surprising gravitational fingerprint is a real level-3 mechanism and sea level is missing from the catalogue, but the page has a single idea and a narrower audience.

build 3: The rigid-Earth sea-level equation is linear in melt, so the fingerprint of each source can be computed offline (spherical-harmonic or Green's-function convolution with an ocean-function iteration) and only scaled in the page; that is honest but the live part is thin. ETOPO is NOAA public domain, while the ice-sheet masks need a named openly licensed source (e.g. BedMachine/IMBIE) that is not yet given.

runnersUp.title: Your pulse
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Counting your own pulse is a lovely hands-on start, but the mechanism is thin and partly covered by heart-circulation's rate control, so it would be stronger folded into a level-0 heart page.

build 3: Heart rate following effort with exponential recovery and a pulse-wave delay is a real but very thin model, and the pulse-counting stopwatch is a tool rather than a model; it risks reading as an animation with sliders.

runnersUp.title: Where sand comes from
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: A good level-0 story, but its size sorting where the river slows repeats river-valleys' deposition and soil-in-a-jar's settling, so it would be better merged with one of them.

build 3: Sternberg's abrasion law and settling speeds by grain size are real but give one exponential and one sort, so as a step-through story it risks being a picture sequence; buildable if the grain sizes along the river are computed from those laws for the chosen rock type.

runnersUp.title: Self-tolerance & autoimmunity
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The two-threshold selection trade-off is a clean mechanism distinct from immune-system's clonal expansion, but the model is thin and close to a single plotted histogram.

build 3: Buildable honestly only if affinity comes from a sequence model, such as the Košmrlj–Chakraborty string-matching model of TCR and peptide. Drawn as independent random numbers, the challenge step becomes circular and the page a toy.

runnersUp.title: Why big birds flap slowly
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: A good everyday question, but the mechanism is a scaling law that a level-0 page must state as 'the sums stop working' rather than show, so it risks being a correlation chart; it is distinct from flight's wing section.

build 3: Pennycuick's scaling formula and the minimum speed from wing loading make a small honest model, but AVONET has mass and wing length and neither wingspan nor wing area, which the formula needs, and the Figshare record shows no clear licence; ship a small table of species with measured span, area and wingbeat frequency (Pennycuick's published tables, or Alerstam et al. 2007, PLoS Biology, CC BY) instead.

runnersUp.title: The liver & drug interactions
judgeNotes: fit-level 2: Extraction ratio and first-pass metabolism are a real mechanism but a narrow extension of pharmacokinetics-dosing in this batch, and it would work better as a section of that page.

build 4: The well-stirred hepatic model and Michaelis–Menten alcohol elimination are closed-form and honest, but the example high- and low-extraction drugs need sourced parameters (e.g. FDA labels, public domain), which the entry does not name.

runnersUp.title: Lighthouses: how far a light can be seen
judgeNotes: fit-level 2: Only the horizon geometry is a mechanism; flash rhythms are a list of conventions, so the page reads more as trivia than how-it-works and sits oddly in earth.

build 4: Geographic range from lamp and eye heights over a curved Earth, plus flash characteristics from the USCG Light List (US-government XML, freely downloadable), is a small honest geometric model; it is thin, so the ship's sighting must be computed from the horizon geometry and not scripted.

runnersUp.title: Choosing a material: composites & Ashby charts
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The Ashby chart is mostly a selection survey with little mechanism; the rule of mixtures and fibre pull-out give it some substance, but it is weaker than the other materials candidates.

build 2: The only real model is the rule of mixtures plus a selection-line ranking; the rest is panning a property chart, close to browsing a diagram, and the data is weak: Materials Project (CC BY 4.0) gives only computed moduli of crystals, so polymers, woods and composites need a hand-compiled table, and the fibre pull-out panel would be a picture.

runnersUp.title: Caterpillar to butterfly
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Appealing and honest for level 0, but it is mostly a staged life-cycle sequence of facts with a weak model (moulting because skin cannot stretch), so less of a toy than its peers.

build 2: Degree-day development (Zalucki 1982 thresholds, facts) and an instar mass curve are real but tiny models. The core of the page is stepping through life-stage drawings and a cutaway of the pupa, which is close to a browse-a-diagram with a temperature multiplier.

runnersUp.title: The placebo effect
judgeNotes: fit-level 2: The Bayesian cue-combination model is normative rather than a mechanism, and its trial-arm half (regression to the mean, natural recovery) duplicates clinical-trials in this batch.

build 3: The Bayesian core is just a precision-weighted mean of two Gaussians, which is thin as an interactive model. The three-arm trial with regression to the mean adds a real simulation, but the conditioning-over-trials part needs a stated learning rule.

runnersUp.title: Ice skates: glide forward, grip sideways
judgeNotes: fit-level 2: Glide along the blade and grip across it is a nice idea, but why ice is slippery is still debated by scientists, so the zoom on a 'thin wet layer' risks teaching something uncertain as fact, and the page mixes a friction survey with blade mechanics.

build 3: The sled comparison is a trivial friction ODE and the blade is an anisotropic-friction rigid body, both buildable, but ice friction coefficients depend on speed and temperature (one cited table must be chosen and named), and the wet-layer zoom is a picture, not a model.

runnersUp.title: Umbrella
judgeNotes: fit-level 2: A simple linkage plus flipping inside out is thin as a 'how it works' subject and weakly linked to anything the site teaches next.

build 3: The runner, stretcher and rib linkage is honest planar kinematics, but turning inside out is snap-through buckling, which a level-0 model can only approximate with a threshold on rib bending, so that part is close to a picture.
